title: Activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT)

review.note: Drafted from the source below; not yet reviewed by a medical professional.

measures: A partial thromboplastin time (PTT) test measures the number of seconds it takes for a blood sample to clot. It checks how many of a specific group of clotting factors a person has and how well they are working.
context: No special preparation is needed for this test. It is often ordered along with a prothrombin time (PT) test, and it may be used to help monitor a blood thinner called heparin. A result outside the usual range does not by itself mean a person has a condition, so more tests may be ordered.
aboveRange: A longer clotting time may be associated with inherited bleeding conditions such as hemophilia or Von Willebrand disease
Liver conditions or a lack of vitamin K
Too much of the blood thinner heparin
Certain autoimmune conditions, which can make the test show a slower clotting time than the body actually has
belowRange: A shorter clotting time can be associated with higher levels of clotting factors, such as during inflammation, pregnancy, or an infection
An early stage of a condition that uses up clotting factors over time
nextStep: Discuss this result with your doctor.
